title: Reading a graph like a chart
objectives: Read the roots and the y-intercept of a curve
Find a turning point and say where a curve is increasing or decreasing
Tell a root, an intercept and a turning point apart

screens.title: Reading a graph like a chart
screens.prose: A chart is only useful if you can read it. A curve has a few landmarks: where it crosses each axis, and where it turns. We will find them by moving along the curve.
This curve is $f(x) = x^2 - 2x - 3$. P rides along it.
screens.question: Drag P to the lowest point of the curve.

hints.text: Move P slowly and watch its y-coordinate. Where does it stop falling?
The lowest point sits halfway between the two places where the curve crosses the x-axis.
The curve crosses the x-axis at −1 and 3. Halfway is $x = 1$, where $f(1) = 1 - 2 - 3 = -4$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep moving P until its height stops falling and starts rising.

byKey.intercept: You stopped where the curve crosses the y-axis, at height −3. Keep going right: the curve dips lower before it turns.
byKey.P: P is not at the bottom yet. Watch its y-coordinate: the lowest value is the one you want.

explain.text: Left of $x = 1$ the curve falls as you move right; after it, the curve rises. The point where it switches, $(1, -4)$, is a **turning point**.

screens.prose: Move P from left to right with the slider. Watch whether its height goes up or down as $x$ grows.
screens.question: For which $x$-values does the curve go down as you move right?

options.why: You picked where the curve sits below the x-axis. That is where the values are negative, not where they fall.
You read the curve from right to left. Read it the way $x$ grows: left to right.
You stopped at the y-axis. The curve keeps falling until $x = 1$.

hints.text: Start P at the far left and slide it right slowly.
Watch P's height as it passes the bottom of the curve.
P's height drops until $x = 1$, then climbs.

feedback.correct: The curve falls all the way to $x = 1$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Slide P left to right and note where its height stops dropping.

explain.text: A curve that goes down as $x$ grows is **decreasing** there; one that goes up is **increasing**. This curve decreases for $x < 1$ and increases for $x > 1$. The turning point is the border between them.

screens.prose: Same curve. It crosses the x-axis twice.
screens.question: Drag A and B onto the two crossings of the x-axis.

hints.text: A crossing of the x-axis has height 0.
One crossing is left of the y-axis, the other right of it.

feedback.correct: A sits at $(-1, 0)$ and B at $(3, 0)$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each point should sit where the curve's height is 0.

byKey.intercept: You put a point where the curve crosses the y-axis. We want the x-axis crossings, at height 0.
byKey.A: A is not on a crossing yet. Drag it until its height is 0.
byKey.B: B is not on a crossing yet. Drag it until its height is 0.

explain.text: The crossings $x = -1$ and $x = 3$ make $f(x) = 0$. They are the **roots** of $f$. A root is an $x$-value, read off the horizontal axis.

screens.prose: The curve also crosses the y-axis, once.
screens.question: At what height does the curve cross the y-axis?

hints.text: The y-axis is the vertical axis. What is $x$ everywhere on it?
Follow the y-axis down until it meets the curve.
On the y-axis $x = 0$, so the height is $f(0) = 0 - 0 - 3 = -3$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the height of the curve at $x = 0$.

byKey.root-left: −1 is a root, where the curve crosses the x-axis. The y-axis is the vertical one, at $x = 0$.
byKey.root-right: 3 is a root, where the curve crosses the x-axis. The y-axis is the vertical one, at $x = 0$.
byKey.turn: −4 is the height of the lowest point, at $x = 1$. The y-axis is at $x = 0$.

explain.text: On the y-axis $x = 0$, so the height is $f(0) = -3$. This is the **y-intercept**. In the rule it is the number with no $x$ attached.

screens.prose: A new curve, $g(x) = 4x - x^2$. It is an upside-down U, so its turning point is a highest point, at $(2, 4)$.
screens.question: Which points are roots of $g$? Select all that apply.

options.why: That is the turning point. A root has height 0.
You dropped straight down from the turning point. The curve is at height 4 there, not 0.

hints.text: A root is where the curve meets the x-axis.
The curve meets the x-axis twice.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Pick every point where the curve meets the x-axis, and only those.

explain.text: The curve meets the x-axis at $x = 0$ and $x = 4$. At the origin it also meets the y-axis. So $(0, 0)$ is a root and the y-intercept at once.

screens.prose: A cubic can turn twice. This is $h(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 4$, with turning points at $(0, 4)$ and $(2, 0)$.
screens.question: Where is $h$ decreasing?

options.why: You picked from the left crossing to the touching point. Decreasing means falling as $x$ grows, which starts at the top, $(0, 4)$.
Those are where it rises. Read left to right: from $(0, 4)$ to $(2, 0)$ the height drops.
$y = x^3$ only rises, but this cubic has two turning points. Between them it must fall.

hints.text: Read left to right, between the two turning points.
Follow the curve from $(0, 4)$ to $(2, 0)$.
From $x = 0$ to $x = 2$ the height drops from 4 to 0, so the curve is decreasing there.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Look for the stretch where the height drops as $x$ grows.

explain.text: Between the turning points the curve falls from 4 to 0; either side of them it rises. At $(2, 0)$ the curve touches the x-axis and turns back. That root is also a turning point.

options.why: You read where the curve crosses the y-axis, at height −2. That is the intercept: it answers $f(0)$, not $f(x) = 0$.
$x = 0$ is where the curve meets the y-axis. There $f(0) = -2$, not 0.
You flipped the signs of the crossings. Check: $f(1) = 1 - 1 - 2 = -2$, not 0.

hints.text: $f(x) = 0$ asks where the height is 0.
Height 0 is the x-axis. Find where the curve crosses it.

feedback.correct: Correct. The curve has height 0 at $x = -1$ and $x = 2$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find where the curve's height is 0.

byKey.b: You read the y-intercept, −2, as a root. A root is an $x$-value where the height is 0, on the x-axis.
byKey.c: You picked the y-axis. That is where $x$ is 0, not where $f(x)$ is 0.

explain.text: Solving $f(x) = 0$ asks where the height is 0: the x-axis crossings, $x = -1$ and $x = 2$. The y-intercept answers a different question, the height at $x = 0$, which is $f(0) = -2$.

screens.prose: You found three landmarks. **Roots** are the $x$-values where the curve crosses the x-axis: they solve $f(x) = 0$. The **y-intercept** is $f(0)$, the height on the y-axis. A **turning point** is where increasing meets decreasing.
screens.question: Use the rule, not a graph. What is the y-intercept of $f(x) = (x - 5)(x + 2)$?

options.why: Those are the roots, read from the brackets. The intercept sets $x = 0$: $(0 - 5)(0 + 2)$.
You dropped a sign: $(-5) \times 2 = -10$.
You added the numbers in the brackets. Multiply them: $(-5)(2)$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Put $x = 0$ into the rule.

screens.prose: An option's **strike** is the price it lets you trade at. Each strike has an **implied volatility**, the swing the market expects. Plotted against strike, these make a **smile**. The share trades at £100.00. Drag P along the smile.
screens.question: At which strike is the implied volatility lowest?

widget.label: Strike with the lowest implied volatility

hints.text: Drag P along the smile and watch its height.
The lowest point of the smile is its turning point.
The smile bottoms out at $(105, 18)$: decreasing before it, increasing after.

feedback.correct: The turning point is at strike £105.00.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the strike, the $x$-value, of the smile's lowest point.

byKey.spot: You assumed the lowest point sits at the share price. Read the graph: it bottoms out to the right of £100.00.
byKey.value: You gave the lowest volatility, 18%. The question asks for the strike: the $x$-value of the turning point.

explain.text: The turning point is at strike £105.00, with implied volatility 18%. The smile decreases for lower strikes and increases for higher ones. Its lowest point need not sit at the share price.

ideas: Roots are the $x$-values where a curve crosses the x-axis: they solve $f(x) = 0$.
The y-intercept is $f(0)$, the height where the curve crosses the y-axis.
Reading left to right, a curve is increasing or decreasing; a turning point is where one meets the other.

formula.name: Three landmarks
formula.note: A root is an $x$-value; an intercept is a height. Only the origin can be both.

summary.trap: Reading the y-intercept as a root: where the curve meets the y-axis gives $f(0)$, not a solution of $f(x) = 0$.

quiz.prose: Here is the graph of a quadratic.
quiz.question: What are its roots?

options.why: −3 is a root, but the curve crosses the x-axis twice. It also crosses at 1.
That is the x of the turning point, where the height is −4, not 0.
$x = 0$ is the y-axis. There the height is −3, not 0.

feedback.correct: The curve crosses the x-axis at −3 and 1.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find every point where the height is 0.

explain.text: The roots are where the curve meets the x-axis: $x = -3$ and $x = 1$. This curve also crosses the y-axis at height −3, which is a different landmark.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Put $x = 0$ into the rule.

byKey.root: 2 is a root, where $y = 0$. The intercept is the height when $x = 0$.
byKey.root-big: 4 is a root, where $y = 0$. The intercept is the height when $x = 0$.
byKey.turn: −1 is the height of the turning point, at $x = 3$. Put $x = 0$ in instead.

explain.text: The y-intercept is the height at $x = 0$. Every term with an $x$ vanishes, leaving the constant, 8.

quiz.prose: A curve has a turning point that is its highest point.
quiz.question: What happens to the curve there, reading left to right?

options.text: It changes from increasing to decreasing
It changes from decreasing to increasing
options.why: That describes a lowest point, the bottom of a U.

options.text: It changes from positive to negative
options.why: Changing sign is crossing the x-axis: a root, not a turn.
A turning point can sit at any height. Height 0 marks a root.

feedback.correct: Up, then down: increasing to decreasing.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Picture the top of an upside-down U.

explain.text: At a highest point the curve stops rising and starts falling. So it changes from increasing to decreasing.

quiz.prose: $f(x) = (x - 2)(x - 6)$ has a U-shaped graph. Its turning point sits halfway between its roots.
quiz.question: What is the $y$-coordinate of the turning point?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the $x$ halfway between the roots, then put it into the rule.

byKey.x: 4 is the $x$-coordinate, halfway between 2 and 6. Now find the height there: $f(4)$.
byKey.int: 12 is the y-intercept, $f(0) = (-2)(-6)$. The turning point is at $x = 4$.

explain.text: The roots are 2 and 6, so the turning point is at $x = 4$. Then $f(4) = (4 - 2)(4 - 6) = -4$. The turning point is $(4, -4)$.
